questions.stem: The forecast says fog is expected to roll in within the hour but visibility is still good. What should the officer of the watch do?
options: Do nothing because visibility is good
Notify the master, because restricted visibility is expected as well as encountered
Wait until the fog actually arrives
Call the master only if the radar fails
questions.explanation: The principles say to notify the master if restricted visibility is encountered or expected. Waiting for the fog to arrive misses the word "expected".

questions.stem: Several vessels are converging at a busy crossing and the officer of the watch is uneasy about them. Which list item applies?
options: Traffic conditions or the movements of other ships are causing concern
Radio equipment malfunction
Heavy weather damage
Failure to obtain soundings
questions.explanation: Concern about traffic or other ships' movements is a listed reason to call the master. The other items are different situations.

questions.stem: During a night watch the helmsman reports that the ship will not hold her course and keeps swinging to port. What should the officer of the watch do?
options: Ignore it since the autopilot is on
Wait until the end of the watch
Tell the helmsman to steer harder and make no further report
Notify the master because difficulty maintaining course and possible steering trouble are on the list, while acting for the ship's safety
questions.explanation: Difficulty in maintaining course, and any steering gear breakdown, are on the list. The officer also takes immediate action for safety. Ignoring or waiting is wrong.

questions.stem: A ship is due to sight a headland light at 2200. At 2230 it is not seen. Which statement is correct?
options: Only call the master if the light is sighted too early
Call the master only in daylight
The officer should notify the master, because failure to sight land or a mark by the expected time is on the list
No action is needed because it may be hidden by haze
questions.explanation: Failure to sight land, a mark or to obtain soundings by the expected time is a trigger. So is land or a mark that appears unexpectedly.

questions.stem: Which of the following equipment failures is a listed reason to notify the master?
options: A broken TV in the crew lounge
A breakdown of the steering gear, an engine or any essential navigational equipment, and a radio malfunction
A failed galley refrigerator
A burned out cabin light
questions.explanation: Engines, propulsion remote control, steering gear, essential navigational equipment and radio malfunction are all listed. Galley, cabin and recreation equipment are not.

questions.stem: In heavy weather, when must the officer of the watch notify the master?
options: If in any doubt about the possibility of weather damage
Only after damage has occurred
Only if wind exceeds 50 knots
Only if the barometer falls
questions.explanation: The principle is to notify if there is any doubt about the possibility of weather damage. It does not set a wind speed, and it does not wait until damage happens.

questions.stem: The look-out reports a drifting log and then a large piece of ice ahead. The officer notes the hazard. Under the principles, what applies?
options: Nothing, since floating objects are normal
Only radar targets must be reported
The master should be informed only if the log hits the ship
A hazard to navigation such as ice or a derelict is a reason to notify the master
questions.explanation: Meeting a hazard to navigation, such as ice or a derelict, is a listed reason to call the master.

questions.stem: A collision looks likely in 30 seconds. The officer of the watch decides to ring the master first and wait for an answer before altering course. What does the principle say?
options: The officer should wait for the rating's opinion
The officer should call the Coast Guard before any action
The officer should not hesitate to take immediate action for the ship's safety, as well as calling the master
The officer should wait for the master's instruction
questions.explanation: Notification does not replace action. The principles say the officer must not hesitate to take immediate action for the safety of the ship where circumstances require.

questions.stem: Why does the list of reasons to call the master end with "any other emergency, or if in any doubt"?
options: Because the master dislikes being called
Because doubt alone is enough reason to call; no proof of danger is needed
Because the list is complete and doubt never applies
Because only emergencies justify a call
questions.explanation: The catch-all sentence makes doubt a reason in itself, so the list cannot be used as an excuse for not calling.

questions.stem: You are the rating on look-out and notice the wheel feels heavy and the steering alarm sounds briefly. What is the best action?
options: Report it to the officer of the watch immediately, because it may be difficulty in maintaining course or a steering problem
Wait to see whether it happens again
Wait until the end of the watch to mention it
Switch the alarm off and say nothing
questions.explanation: Report steering warning signs at once. The officer decides whether it is a trigger for calling the master. Waiting, staying silent or switching off an alarm are unsafe.
